sentences.zh: 突厥 吐谷渾 高昌 鄯善 焉耆 龜茲 于闐 囐噠 粟特 安息 波斯

translations.literal: Turks, Tuyuhun, Gaochang, Shanshan, Karasahr, Kucha, Khotan, Hephtalites, Sogdia, Parthia, Persia
translations.idiomatic: The Turks; Tuyuhun; Gaochang; Shanshan; Karasahr; Kucha; Khotan; the Hephtalites; Sogdia; Parthia; and Persia

sentences.zh: 突厥者，蓋匈奴之別種，姓阿史那氏。

translations.literal: The Turks were in general a separate branch of the Xiongnu, surnamed Ashina.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were essentially a distinct offshoot of the Xiongnu, bearing the clan name Ashina.

sentences.zh: 別為部落。

translations.literal: They were split off as a separate tribe.
translations.idiomatic: They had broken away to form their own tribe.

sentences.zh: 後為鄰國所破，盡滅其族。

translations.literal: Later they were broken by a neighboring state and their entire clan was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Later a neighboring power defeated them and wiped out the whole clan.

sentences.zh: 有一兒，年且十歲，兵人見其小，不忍殺之，乃刖其足，棄草澤中。

translations.literal: There was one boy, nearly ten years old; the soldiers, seeing he was small, could not bear to kill him, so they cut off his feet and abandoned him in the reedy marshes.
translations.idiomatic: One boy of about ten was spared because the soldiers thought him too young to kill; instead they maimed his feet and left him in the marshlands.

sentences.zh: 有牝狼以肉飼之，及長，與狼合，遂有孕焉。

translations.literal: A she-wolf fed him with meat; when he grew up he united with the wolf and she became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: A she-wolf brought him meat, and when he grew to manhood he coupled with her and she conceived.

sentences.zh: 彼王聞此兒尚在，重遣殺之。

translations.literal: That king, hearing this child was still alive, again sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When that king learned the boy still lived, he sent assassins again.

sentences.zh: 使者見狼在側，並欲殺狼。

translations.literal: The envoy, seeing the wolf at his side, wished to kill the wolf as well.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy, finding the wolf beside him, meant to kill the wolf too.

sentences.zh: 狼遂逃于高昌國之北山。

translations.literal: The wolf thereupon fled to the northern mountains of the state of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: The wolf fled to the mountains north of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 山有洞穴，穴內有平壤茂草，周回數百里，四面俱山。

translations.literal: The mountain had a cave; within the cave were level ground and lush grass, several hundred li in circuit, mountains on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountain was a cave with level ground and thick grass, encompassing several hundred li and walled in on every side.

sentences.zh: 狼匿其中，遂生十男。

translations.literal: The wolf hid within it and thereupon bore ten sons.
translations.idiomatic: The wolf hid there and bore ten sons.

sentences.zh: 十男長大，外託妻孕，其後各有一姓，阿史那卽一也。

translations.literal: When the ten sons grew up, they took wives from outside; afterward each had a separate surname, and Ashina was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: When the ten sons came of age they married women from outside; each line then took a surname of its own, and Ashina was one.

sentences.zh: 子孫蕃育，漸至數百家。

translations.literal: Their descendants multiplied and gradually reached several hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Their descendants multiplied until they numbered several hundred households.

sentences.zh: 經數世，相與出穴，臣於茹茹。

translations.literal: After several generations they came forth from the cave together and submitted to the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: After several generations they left the cave together and became subjects of the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 居金山之陽，為茹茹鐵工。

translations.literal: They dwelt on the southern slopes of the Altai and served the Rouran as ironworkers.
translations.idiomatic: They lived on the southern face of the Altai and worked iron for the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 金山形似兜鍪，其俗謂兜鍪為「突厥」，遂因以為號焉。

translations.literal: The Altai resembles a helmet; in their custom a helmet is called "Tujue," and so they took it as their name.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain resembled a war helmet, which in their tongue was called "Turk"; they took that word as their tribal name.

sentences.zh: 或云突厥之先出於索國，在匈奴之北。

translations.literal: Some say the ancestors of the Turks came forth from the state of Suo, north of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Others hold that the Turks' forebears issued from the land of Suo, north of the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 其部落大人曰阿謗步，兄弟十七人。

translations.literal: The great man of their tribe was named A-bo-bu, and he had seventeen brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribal leader was called A-bo-bu, who had seventeen brothers.

sentences.zh: 其一曰伊質泥師都，狼所生也。

translations.literal: One of them was named Yi-zhi Ni-shi-du, born of a wolf.
translations.idiomatic: One brother was Yi-zhi Ni-shi-du, said to be born of a wolf.

sentences.zh: 謗步等性竝愚癡，國遂被滅。

translations.literal: Bo-bu and the others were by nature all foolish and dull, and the state was thereupon destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Bo-bu and his brothers were all dull-witted by nature, and their polity was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 泥師都旣別感異氣，能徵召風雨。

translations.literal: Ni-shi-du alone had received a strange emanation and could summon wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Ni-shi-du alone was touched by an uncanny force and could call up wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 娶二妻，云是夏神、冬神之女也。

translations.literal: He took two wives, saying they were daughters of the Summer God and the Winter God.
translations.idiomatic: He married two wives, declaring them daughters of the gods of summer and winter.

sentences.zh: 一孕而生四男。

translations.literal: In one pregnancy she bore four sons.
translations.idiomatic: One wife conceived and bore four sons at once.

sentences.zh: 其一變為白鴻；

translations.literal: One of them transformed into a white swan;
translations.idiomatic: One son turned into a white swan;

sentences.zh: 其一國于阿輔水、劔水之間，號為契骨；

translations.literal: one established a state between the Afu River and the Jian River, called Qigu;
translations.idiomatic: one founded a realm between the Afu and Jian rivers, called Qigu;

sentences.zh: 其一國於處折水；

translations.literal: one established a state on the Chuzhe River;
translations.idiomatic: one settled on the Chuzhe River;

sentences.zh: 其一居踐斯處折施山，卽其大兒也。

translations.literal: one dwelt on Mount Jiansi-Chuzhe-Shi—that was the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: one lived on Mount Jiansi-Chuzhe-Shi—this was the eldest son.

sentences.zh: 山上仍有阿謗步種類，竝多寒露。

translations.literal: On the mountain there still remained the stock of A-bo-bu, and they were all much afflicted by cold dew.
translations.idiomatic: On the mountain the descendants of A-bo-bu still lived, all suffering grievously from cold dew.

sentences.zh: 大兒為出火溫養之，咸得全濟。

translations.literal: The eldest son went out and warmed them with fire, and all were fully saved.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son went forth and warmed them with fire until all were restored.

sentences.zh: 遂共奉大兒為主，號為突厥，卽訥都六設也。

translations.literal: They thereupon together enthroned the eldest son as lord, styled Turk—that is, Ne-du-liu She.
translations.idiomatic: They then jointly installed the eldest son as ruler, styled Turk—namely Ne-du-liu She.

sentences.zh: 訥都六有十妻，所生子皆以母族為姓，阿史那是其小妻之子也。

translations.literal: Ne-du-liu had ten wives; the sons born to him all took their mothers' clans as surnames, and Ashina was the son of his junior wife.
translations.idiomatic: Ne-du-liu had ten wives; each son took his mother's clan as surname, and Ashina was born to the youngest wife.

sentences.zh: 訥都六死，十母子內欲擇立一人，乃相率於大樹下，共為約曰，向樹跳躍，能最高者，卽推立之。

translations.literal: When Ne-du-liu died, the ten mothers and sons within wished to choose one to install; they gathered together under a great tree and made a pact, saying: whoever jumps toward the tree and can jump highest shall be pushed forward to be installed.
translations.idiomatic: After Ne-du-liu's death the ten mothers and their sons sought to choose a successor; they met under a great tree and agreed that whoever leaped highest toward it would be made chief.

sentences.zh: 阿史那子年幼而跳最高者，諸子遂奉以為主，號阿賢設。

translations.literal: The Ashina son was young, yet he jumped highest; the sons thereupon enthroned him as lord, styled A-xian She.
translations.idiomatic: The Ashina boy, though young, leaped highest; the brothers therefore enthroned him as A-xian She.

sentences.zh: 此說雖殊，然終狼種也。

translations.literal: Although this account differs, in the end they were still wolf stock.
translations.idiomatic: Though the two accounts differ, both trace the line to wolf descent.

sentences.zh: 其後曰土門，部落稍盛，始至塞上市繒絮，願通中國。

translations.literal: Afterward came Tu-men; the tribe gradually grew stronger and first came to the frontier markets to sell silk floss, wishing to open relations with China.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Tu-men; as the tribe grew they began selling silk floss at the frontier markets and sought ties with China.

sentences.zh: 大統十一年，太祖遣酒泉胡安諾盤陀使焉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Datong, the Grand Ancestor sent the Jiuquan Hu An-nuo Pan-tuo as envoy there.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Datong (545), the Grand Ancestor sent An-nuo Pan-tuo, a Hu from Jiuquan, as envoy.

sentences.zh: 其國皆相慶曰：「今大國使至，我國將興也。

translations.literal: The whole state rejoiced together, saying: "Now an envoy of the great state has come—our state will rise."
translations.idiomatic: The whole realm rejoiced, saying, "An envoy from the great power has arrived—our state will flourish."

sentences.zh: 」十二年，土門遂遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth year, Tu-men then sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Tu-men sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 時鐵勒將伐茹茹，土門率所部邀擊，破之，盡降其衆五萬餘落。

translations.literal: At that time the Tiele were about to attack the Rouran; Tu-men led his division to intercept them, defeated them, and wholly reduced their masses of more than fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tiele prepared to attack the Rouran, Tu-men intercepted them, routed them, and absorbed more than fifty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 恃其強盛，乃求婚於茹茹。

translations.literal: Relying on his growing strength, he then asked for a marriage alliance with the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: Emboldened by his strength, he sought a marriage alliance with the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 茹茹主阿那瑰大怒，使人罵辱之曰：「爾是我鍛奴，何敢發是言也？

translations.literal: The Rouran ruler Anagui was greatly angered and sent a man to revile and insult him, saying: "You are my iron-smith slave—how dare you utter such words?"
translations.idiomatic: Rouran ruler Anagui flew into a rage and sent a messenger to revile him: "You are my forge slave—how dare you speak thus?"

sentences.zh: 」土門亦怒，殺其使者。

translations.literal: " Tu-men was also angry and killed their envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Tu-men in turn killed the envoy.

sentences.zh: 遂與之絕，而求婚於我。

translations.literal: He thereupon broke with them and asked to marry into our state.
translations.idiomatic: He broke with the Rouran and sought a marriage alliance with us.

sentences.zh: 太祖許之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，以魏長樂公主妻之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year, the Princess Chang-le of Wei was given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year seventeen (553) the Princess Chang-le of Wei was given him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏文帝崩，土門遣使來弔，贈馬二百匹。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Wen of Wei died; Tu-men sent envoys to offer condolences and presented two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Wen of Wei died; Tu-men sent mourners and two hundred horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 科羅號乙息記可汗。

translations.literal: Ke-luo was styled Yi-xi-ji Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Ke-luo took the title Yi-xi-ji Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 又破叔子於沃野北木賴山。

translations.literal: He again defeated Shuzi north of Woye at Mount Mu-lai.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Shuzi north of Woye at Mount Mu-lai.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，科羅遣使獻馬五萬匹。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, Ke-luo sent envoys presenting fifty thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year two Ke-luo sent fifty thousand horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 科羅死，弟俟斤立，號木汗可汗。

translations.literal: Ke-luo died; his younger brother Hou-jin succeeded, styled Mu-han Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: When Ke-luo died his younger brother Hou-jin succeeded as Mu-han Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 俟斤一名燕都，狀貌多奇異，面廣尺餘，其色甚赤，眼若瑠璃。

translations.literal: Hou-jin, also named Yan-du, had a most unusual appearance: his face was more than a foot wide, exceedingly red in color, and his eyes were like glass.
translations.idiomatic: Hou-jin, also called Yan-du, looked striking—his face was over a foot across, deeply ruddy, and his eyes like glass.

sentences.zh: 性剛暴，務於征伐。

translations.literal: By nature he was fierce and violent and devoted himself to campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce by nature, he lived for war.

sentences.zh: 乃率兵擊鄧叔子，滅之。

translations.literal: He then led troops to attack Deng Shuzi and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Deng Shuzi and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 叔子以其餘燼來奔。

translations.literal: Shuzi came fleeing with his remaining embers.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzi fled with the remnants of his force.

sentences.zh: 俟斤又西破囐噠，東走契丹，北幷契骨，威服塞外諸國。

translations.literal: Hou-jin again defeated the Hephtalites in the west, drove the Khitan eastward, annexed Qigu in the north, and awed into submission all the states beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Hou-jin crushed the Hephtalites in the west, drove the Khitan east, absorbed Qigu in the north, and overawed the frontier states.

sentences.zh: 其地東自遼海以西，西至西海萬里，南自沙漠以北，北至北海五六千里，皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Their territory extended from the Liao Sea in the east to the Western Sea ten thousand li away in the west, and from the desert in the south to the Northern Sea five or six thousand li in the north—all came under them.
translations.idiomatic: Their domain ran from the Liao Sea westward ten thousand li to the Western Sea, and from the desert northward five or six thousand li to the Northern Sea—all submitted.

sentences.zh: 其俗被髮左衽，穹廬氈帳，隨水草遷徙，以畜牧射獵為務。

translations.literal: Their custom was to wear disheveled hair and garments with the left lapel outer; they lived in domed felt tents and moved with grass and water, taking herding and hunting as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: They wore their hair loose and garments left-lapped, dwelt in felt domes, followed pasture and water, and lived by herding and the hunt.

sentences.zh: 賤老貴壯，寡廉恥，無禮義，猶古之匈奴也。

translations.literal: They despised the old and honored the strong, were devoid of modesty and shame, without ritual propriety—much like the Xiongnu of old.
translations.idiomatic: They scorned age, prized strength, lacked shame or ritual decorum—much like the ancient Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 其主初立，近侍重臣等輿之以氈，隨日轉九回，每一回，臣下皆拜。

translations.literal: When their ruler was first installed, close attendants and great ministers carried him on felt and turned him with the sun nine revolutions; at each revolution the ministers all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: At a new khan's installation, close ministers lifted him on felt and turned him nine times with the sun; at each turn the court bowed.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，乃扶令乘馬，以帛絞其頸，使纔不至絕，然後釋而急問之曰：「你能作幾年可汗？

translations.literal: When the bowing was finished, they supported him onto a horse, strangled his neck with silk so that it barely did not break, then released him and urgently asked: "How many years can you be qaghan?"
translations.idiomatic: After the bows they set him on a horse, looped silk about his neck until he nearly suffocated, then asked urgently, "How many years will you reign as qaghan?"

sentences.zh: 」其主旣神情瞀亂，不能詳定多少。

translations.literal: " The ruler, his spirit already clouded and confused, could not state clearly how many.
translations.idiomatic: Dazed from strangulation, the khan could give no clear number.

sentences.zh: 臣下等隨其所言，以驗修短之數。

translations.literal: The ministers and others followed whatever he said to verify the length or shortness of his span.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers took whatever number he gasped as the prophecy of his reign.

sentences.zh: 大官有葉護，次

translations.literal: Among the great offices was the Yabghu, next
translations.idiomatic: Senior offices included the yabghu, then

translations.literal: text missing in manuscript
translations.idiomatic: lacuna in manuscript

sentences.zh: 〔設〕，次特

translations.literal: [supplied: She], next the Te
translations.idiomatic: [emended: she-rank], then the te-

translations.literal: supplied character le
translations.idiomatic: emended: le, completing the rank name tegin

sentences.zh: 〔勤〕，次俟利發，次吐屯發，及餘小官凡二十八等，皆世為之。

translations.literal: [supplied: qin], next Irbiliq, next Tutun-fa, and the remaining lesser offices totaling twenty-eight grades, all hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: [emended: qin-rank], then irbiliq, then tutun, and lesser posts to twenty-eight grades in all, all hereditary.

sentences.zh: 兵器有弓矢鳴鏑甲矟刀劔，其佩飾則兼有伏突。

translations.literal: Their weapons included bows, arrows, whistling arrowheads, armor, spears, swords, and blades; their belt ornaments also included the futu dagger.
translations.idiomatic: They bore bow, arrow, whistling-bolt, armor, spear, sword, and blade; belt gear also included the futu dagger.

sentences.zh: 旗纛之上，施金狼頭。

translations.literal: On flags and banners they affixed golden wolf heads.
translations.idiomatic: Standards bore gilded wolf heads.

sentences.zh: 侍衛之士，謂之附離，夏言亦狼也。

translations.literal: The guards were called fuli—in Chinese speech this also means wolf.
translations.idiomatic: Royal guards were called fuli—"wolf" in their tongue.

sentences.zh: 蓋本狼生，志不忘舊。

translations.literal: It was because they were born of wolves that their will did not forget the old.
translations.idiomatic: Born of wolves, they never forgot that origin.

sentences.zh: 其徵發兵馬，科稅雜畜，輒刻木為數，幷一金鏃箭，蠟封印之，以為信契。

translations.literal: When they mobilized troops and horses and levied taxes in miscellaneous livestock, they carved wood for the count and also used a gold arrowhead sealed in wax as the token of covenant.
translations.idiomatic: To levy troops or livestock tribute they carved tallies in wood and sealed a gold arrowhead in wax as the bond of trust.

sentences.zh: 其刑法：反叛、殺人及姦人之婦、盜馬絆者，皆死；

translations.literal: Their penal code: rebellion, murder, adultery with another man's wife, and stealing horse hobbles—all were death;
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes included rebellion, murder, adultery with another man's wife, and stealing horse hobbles;

sentences.zh: 姦人女者，重責財物，卽以其女妻之；

translations.literal: adultery with an unmarried woman incurred heavy fines in goods, and he was given the woman as wife;
translations.idiomatic: seduction of an unmarried woman brought heavy fines, and the seducer married her;

sentences.zh: 鬬傷人者，隨輕重輸物；

translations.literal: those who wounded in brawls paid goods according to severity;
translations.idiomatic: brawlers paid compensation scaled to the injury;

sentences.zh: 盜馬及雜物者，各十餘倍徵之。

translations.literal: horse thieves and thieves of miscellaneous goods were each mulcted more than tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: theft of horses or goods was fined at more than ten times the value.

sentences.zh: 死者，停屍於帳，子孫及諸親屬男女，各殺羊馬，陳於帳前，祭之。

translations.literal: When someone died, the corpse was left in the tent; sons, grandsons, and all relatives male and female each slaughtered sheep and horses and set them out before the tent as offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The dead lay in the tent while kin of both sexes slaughtered sheep and horses before it as offerings.

sentences.zh: 繞帳走馬七匝，一詣帳門，以刀剺面，且哭，血淚俱流，如此者七度，乃止。

translations.literal: They circled the tent running horses seven circuits; each time they came to the tent door they cut their faces with a knife and wept, blood and tears flowing together—thus seven times, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Mourners rode seven circuits around the tent, and at each pass cut their faces at the door until blood and tears mingled—seven times in all.

sentences.zh: 擇日，取亡者所乘馬及經服用之物，幷屍俱焚之，收其餘灰，待時而葬。

translations.literal: On a chosen day they took the horse the dead had ridden and the objects he had used in life, together with the corpse, and burned them all; they gathered the remaining ashes and awaited the season for burial.
translations.idiomatic: On the chosen day they burned the dead man's horse, goods, and body together, collected the ashes, and waited for burial season.

sentences.zh: 春夏死者，候草木黃落，秋冬死者，候華葉榮茂，然始坎而瘞之。

translations.literal: Those who died in spring and summer waited until grass and trees yellowed and fell; those who died in autumn and winter waited until flowers and leaves flourished luxuriantly—only then did they dig a pit and inter them.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and summer deaths were buried when foliage yellowed; autumn and winter deaths when leaves flourished again.

sentences.zh: 葬之日，親屬設祭，及走馬剺面，如初死之儀。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, relatives set out offerings and ran horses and cut their faces as at the first death rites.
translations.idiomatic: Burial day repeated the running of horses and face-cutting of the first mourning.

sentences.zh: 葬訖，於墓所立石建標。

translations.literal: When burial was finished, they erected stone markers at the grave site.
translations.idiomatic: After burial they raised stone pillars at the grave.

sentences.zh: 其石多少，依平生所殺人數。

translations.literal: How many stones depended on the number of men he had killed in life.
translations.idiomatic: The number of stones matched the men he had slain in life.

sentences.zh: 又以祭之羊馬頭，盡懸掛於標上。

translations.literal: They also hung the heads of sheep and horses offered in sacrifice, all suspended on the markers.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial sheep and horse heads were hung on the markers.

sentences.zh: 是日也，男女咸盛服飾，會於葬所。

translations.literal: On that day men and women all wore splendid dress and gathered at the burial place.
translations.idiomatic: That day all assembled at the grave in full finery.

sentences.zh: 男有悅愛於女者，歸卽遣人娉問，其父母多不違也。

translations.literal: If a man took a liking to a woman, he would return and send someone to ask for betrothal; her parents mostly did not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: A man who desired a woman sent betrothal envoys, and parents seldom refused.

sentences.zh: 父〔兄〕伯叔死者，子弟及侄等妻其後母、世叔母及嫂，唯尊者不得下淫。

translations.literal: When father, [elder] brother, uncle, or paternal uncle died, sons, younger brothers, nephews, and the like married the deceased's stepmother, father's younger brother's wife, or sister-in-law—only one may not lie with a superior.
translations.idiomatic: After a father's or elder brother's death, sons and nephews might marry the widow, a junior uncle's wife, or a sister-in-law—never a superior's wife.

sentences.zh: 雖移徙無常，而各有地分。

translations.literal: Although they moved without fixed abode, each still had his allotted territory.
translations.idiomatic: Though nomadic, each clan held its own pasture.

sentences.zh: 可汗恆處於都斤山，牙帳東開，蓋敬日之所出也。

translations.literal: The qaghan constantly resided at Mount Du-jin; the royal tent opened to the east, honoring the place where the sun comes forth.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan dwelt on Mount Du-jin; his tent faced east toward the sunrise.

sentences.zh: 每歲率諸貴人，祭其先窟。

translations.literal: Each year he led the nobles to sacrifice at their ancestral cave.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he led nobles to sacrifice at the ancestral cave.

sentences.zh: 又以五月中旬，集他人水，拜祭天神。

translations.literal: Also in the middle of the fifth month they gathered at another's water to bow and sacrifice to the Heaven God.
translations.idiomatic: In mid-fifth month they assembled at sacred waters to worship Heaven.

sentences.zh: 於都斤四五百里，有高山迥出，上無草樹，謂其為勃登凝黎，夏言地神也。

translations.literal: Four or five hundred li from Du-jin a high mountain rose abruptly, bare of grass and trees; they called it Bo-deng Ning-li—in Chinese speech, the Earth God.
translations.idiomatic: Four or five hundred li from Du-jin stood a bare peak they called Bo-deng Ning-li—the Earth God.

sentences.zh: 其書字類胡，而不知年曆，唯以草青為記。

translations.literal: Their script resembled that of the Hu, but they did not know the calendar and reckoned only by the greening of grass.
translations.idiomatic: Their writing resembled Hu script; they knew no calendar and marked time only when grass turned green.

sentences.zh: 俟斤部衆旣盛，乃遣使請誅鄧叔子等。

translations.literal: Hou-jin's following had grown mighty; he then sent envoys requesting the execution of Deng Shuzi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: As Hou-jin's power grew he asked permission to execute Deng Shuzi and his party.

sentences.zh: 太祖許之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor agreed.

sentences.zh: 收叔子以下三千人，付其使者，殺之於青門外。

translations.literal: Shuzi and the more than three thousand below him were taken and handed to his envoy and killed outside the Green Gate.
translations.idiomatic: We delivered Shuzi and three thousand followers to his envoys, who executed them outside the Green Gate.

sentences.zh: 三年，俟斤襲擊吐谷渾，破之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Hou-jin attacked Tuyuhun and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Hou-jin attacked Tuyuhun and routed them.

sentences.zh: 語在《吐谷渾傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Tuyuhun."
translations.idiomatic: The fuller account appears in the Biography of Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 明帝二年，俟斤遣使來獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Ming, Hou-jin sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming's second year Hou-jin sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，又三輩遣使貢其方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, they again sent three missions presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding (561) they sent three embassies with tribute.

sentences.zh: 時與齊人交爭，戎車歲動，故每連結之，以為外援。

translations.literal: At that time they were contending with the Qi; war-chariots moved every year, so they constantly allied with the Turks as an external aid.
translations.idiomatic: They were at war with Qi year after year, so the court repeatedly courted the Turks as an outside ally.

sentences.zh: 初，魏恭帝世，俟斤許進女于太祖，契未定而太祖崩。

translations.literal: In the beginning, in the era of Emperor Gong of Wei, Hou-jin had promised to send a daughter to the Grand Ancestor, but the pact was not settled when the Grand Ancestor died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gong's reign Hou-jin had pledged a daughter to the Grand Ancestor, but the Grand Ancestor died before the match was sealed.

sentences.zh: 尋而俟斤又以他女許高祖，未及結納，齊人亦遣求婚，俟斤貪其幣厚，將悔之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Hou-jin again promised another daughter to Emperor Gaozu; before the marriage was concluded the Qi also sent to ask for marriage; Hou-jin, greedy for their thick gifts, was about to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Hou-jin soon promised another daughter to Emperor Gaozu; before the wedding Qi too sought a bride, and Hou-jin, tempted by richer Qi gifts, nearly reneged.

sentences.zh: 至是，詔遣涼州刺史楊薦、武伯王慶等往結之。

translations.literal: At this time an edict sent Liangzhou Inspector Yang Jian, Martial Baron Wang Qing, and others to conclude the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: The court then dispatched Yang Jian, governor of Liangzhou, Wang Qing, Martial Baron, and others to bind the alliance.

sentences.zh: 慶等至，諭以信義。

translations.literal: When Qing and the others arrived, they instructed him in faith and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and his party arrived and pressed the bond of trust.

sentences.zh: 俟斤遂絕齊使而訂婚焉。

translations.literal: Hou-jin thereupon cut off the Qi envoys and fixed the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Hou-jin broke with Qi envoys and confirmed the betrothal.

sentences.zh: 仍請舉國東伐。

translations.literal: He still requested to lead the whole state in an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to march east with his entire nation.

sentences.zh: 語在薦等傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the biographies of Jian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller account appears in the biographies of Jian and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔隨公楊忠率衆一萬，與突厥伐齊。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered Duke of Sui Yang Zhong to lead ten thousand men to campaign against Qi with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the court ordered Duke of Sui Yang Zhong with ten thousand troops to join the Turks against Qi.

sentences.zh: 忠軍度陘嶺，俟斤率騎十萬來會。

translations.literal: Zhong's army crossed Long Ridge; Hou-jin led one hundred thousand horsemen to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong crossed Long Ridge; Hou-jin brought one hundred thousand cavalry to the rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，攻齊主於晉陽，不剋。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year they attacked the Qi ruler at Jinyang but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The next first month they assaulted the Qi ruler at Jinyang but failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 俟斤遂縱兵大掠而還。

translations.literal: Hou-jin thereupon let his troops loose in great plunder and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hou-jin then unleashed his men in wide plunder and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 忠言於高祖曰：「突厥甲兵惡，爵賞輕，首領多而無法令，何謂難制馭。

translations.literal: Zhong said to Emperor Gaozu: "The Turks' armor and weapons are harsh, their titles and rewards light, their chiefs many and without statutes—why speak of difficulty in controlling them?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong told Emperor Gaozu, "Turk arms are fierce but rewards cheap; chiefs are many and lawless—why call them hard to master?"

sentences.zh: 正由比者使人妄道其彊盛，欲令國家厚其使者，身往重取其報。

translations.literal: It is just because lately envoys falsely spoke of their strength, wishing to make the state enrich their envoys so that they themselves going there might heavily take repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys lately lied about Turk might so the court would lavish gifts they could pocket on return.

sentences.zh: 朝廷受其虛言，將士望風畏懾。

translations.literal: The court accepted their empty words; officers and soldiers feared them at sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed the flattery; soldiers quailed at the rumor.

sentences.zh: 但虜態詐健，而實易與耳。

translations.literal: But the barbarians' manner is deceitful and hardy, while in truth they are easy to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: The nomads bluster, yet in fact they are easy to handle.

sentences.zh: 今以臣觀之，前後使人皆可斬也。

translations.literal: Now as I see it, the envoys before and after may all be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: In my view every envoy who overstated them deserves execution."

sentences.zh: 」高祖不納。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，俟斤復遣使來獻，更請東伐。

translations.literal: That year Hou-jin again sent envoys presenting tribute and again requested an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hou-jin sent tribute again and renewed his plea for an eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔楊忠率兵出沃野，晉公護趣洛陽以應之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yang Zhong to lead troops out from Woye; Duke of Jin Hu hurried to Luoyang to respond.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Yang Zhong out from Woye while Duke of Jin Hu raced to Luoyang in support.

sentences.zh: 會護戰不利，俟斤引還。

translations.literal: As Hu's battle went ill, Hou-jin led his forces back.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu's campaign faltered, Hou-jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔陳公純、大司徒宇文貴、神武公竇毅、南安公楊薦等往逆女。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered Duke of Chen Chun, Grand Minister of State Yuwen Gui, Martial Duke Dou Yi, Duke of Nan'an Yang Jian, and others to go to meet the bride.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Duke of Chen Chun, Yuwen Gui, Dou Yi, Yang Jian, and others were sent to escort the bride.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，俟斤又遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, Hou-jin again sent envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe Hou-jin sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 陳公純等至，俟斤復貳於齊。

translations.literal: When Duke of Chen Chun and the others arrived, Hou-jin again wavered toward Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Chun's party arrived Hou-jin again leaned toward Qi.

sentences.zh: 會有風雷變，乃許純等以后歸。

translations.literal: There occurred wind and thunder changes; he then promised Chun and the others to send the queen later.
translations.idiomatic: A storm omen moved him to promise Chun the bride would follow later.

sentences.zh: 語在《皇后傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of the Empress."
translations.idiomatic: The account appears in the Biography of the Empress.

sentences.zh: 四年，俟斤又遣使獻馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Hou-jin again sent envoys presenting horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Hou-jin sent horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 俟斤死，弟他缽可汗立。

translations.literal: Hou-jin died; his younger brother Ta-bo Qaghan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Hou-jin died; his brother Ta-bo became qaghan.

sentences.zh: 自俟斤以來，其國富彊，有淩轢中夏志。

translations.literal: From Hou-jin onward their state was rich and strong, with the will to overrun the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hou-jin the Turks had grown rich and bold enough to dream of dominating China.

sentences.zh: 朝廷旣與和親，歲給繒絮錦彩十萬段。

translations.literal: The court, having made peace by marriage, each year gave one hundred thousand bolts of silk floss, brocade, and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: Once allied by marriage the court sent one hundred thousand bolts of silk and brocade yearly.

sentences.zh: 突厥在京師者，又待以優禮，衣錦食肉者，常以千數。

translations.literal: Turks in the capital were also treated with preferential rites; those clothed in brocade eating meat often numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Turks resident in the capital lived in luxury—thousands clad in brocade and fed on meat.

sentences.zh: 齊人懼其寇掠，亦傾府藏以給之。

translations.literal: The Qi, fearing their raids, also emptied their treasuries to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, fearing Turk raids, likewise drained their treasury to pay them.

sentences.zh: 他缽彌復驕傲，至乃率其徒屬曰：「但使我在南兩個兒孝順，何憂無物邪。

translations.literal: Ta-bo became arrogant again; he even led his followers saying: "So long as my two sons in the south are filial, why worry about lacking goods?"
translations.idiomatic: Ta-bo grew haughty again, telling his followers, "If my two southern sons stay dutiful, goods will never run short."

sentences.zh: 」建德二年，他缽遣使獻馬。

translations.literal: " In the second year of Jiande, Ta-bo sent envoys presenting horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiande Ta-bo sent horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾，本遼東鮮卑慕容廆之庶兄也。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun were originally the younger brother by a concubine of Murong Hui of the Liaodong Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun sprang from Murong Hui's younger half-brother among the Liaodong Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 初，吐谷渾馬與廆馬鬥而廆馬傷，廆遣讓之。

translations.literal: In the beginning, Tuyuhun's horse fought with Hui's horse and Hui's horse was injured; Hui sent to reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tuyuhun's stallion fought Hui's and wounded it; Hui rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾怒，率其部落去之，止于枹罕，自為君長。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun was angry, led his tribe and left, stopping at Fuhan and making himself clan leader.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Tuyuhun led his people away to Fuhan and declared himself their chief.

sentences.zh: 及孫葉延，頗視書傳。

translations.literal: By the time of his grandson Ye-yan, he quite looked into books and records.
translations.idiomatic: By his grandson Ye-yan's day the line had taken up learning.

sentences.zh: 以古有王父字為氏，遂以吐谷渾為氏焉。

translations.literal: Because antiquity took the grandfather's character as clan name, they thereupon took Tuyuhun as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Following the ancient custom of taking a forebear's name as surname, they adopted Tuyuhun as their clan.

sentences.zh: 自吐谷渾至伏連籌一十四世。

translations.literal: From Tuyuhun to Fu-lian-chou was fourteen generations.
translations.idiomatic: From Tuyuhun to Fu-lian-chou stretched fourteen generations.

sentences.zh: 伏連籌死，子夸呂立，始自號為可汗。

translations.literal: When Fu-lian-chou died, his son Kua-lu succeeded and first styled himself qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu-lian-chou's son Kua-lu succeeded and first took the title qaghan.

sentences.zh: 治伏俟城，在青海西十五里。

translations.literal: He ruled from Fu-hou City, fifteen li west of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: His seat was Fu-hou City, fifteen li west of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 雖有城郭，而不居之，恆處穹廬，隨水草畜牧。

translations.literal: Although they had walls and towns, they did not dwell in them, constantly staying in domed tents and herding with grass and water.
translations.idiomatic: They built towns yet lived in felt tents, moving with pasture and water.

sentences.zh: 其地東西三千里，南北千餘里。

translations.literal: Their territory was three thousand li east to west and more than a thousand li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm measured three thousand li east-west and over a thousand li north-south.

sentences.zh: 官有王公、僕射、尚書及郎中、將軍之號。

translations.literal: Offices included king, duke, puye, shangshu, and the titles langzhong and general.
translations.idiomatic: Their bureaucracy ran from king and duke through puye, shangshu, langzhong, and general.

sentences.zh: 夸呂椎髻、毦、珠，以皂為帽，坐金師子床。

translations.literal: Kua-lu wore a topknot, felt, and pearls, used black for his cap, and sat on a golden lion couch.
translations.idiomatic: Kua-lu topknotted his hair, wore felt and pearls, a black cap, and a golden lion throne.

sentences.zh: 號其妻為恪尊，衣織成裙，披錦大袍，辮發於後，首戴金花。

translations.literal: He styled his wife Ke-zun; she wore woven skirts, draped brocade great robes, braided her hair behind, and wore golden flowers on her head.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was called Ke-zun, in woven skirts and brocade cloaks, hair braided back, head crowned with gold flowers.

sentences.zh: 其俗丈夫衣服略同於華夏，多以羃羅為冠，亦以繒為帽。

translations.literal: Their custom: men's dress was much like that of the Central States; many used felt gauze for caps, and also used silk for hats.
translations.idiomatic: Men dressed much like Chinese subjects, often in felt caps or silk hats.

sentences.zh: 婦人皆貫珠束發，以多為貴。

translations.literal: Women all threaded pearls in their hair, taking abundance as honor.
translations.idiomatic: Women threaded pearls through their hair—the more pearls, the higher the status.

sentences.zh: 兵器有弓刀甲矟。

translations.literal: Weapons included bow, blade, armor, and spear.
translations.idiomatic: Their arms were bow, sword, armor, and spear.

sentences.zh: 國無常賦，須則稅富室商人以充用焉。

translations.literal: The state had no fixed levies; when need arose they taxed wealthy households and merchants to fill use.
translations.idiomatic: There was no standing tax; needs were met by levies on rich merchants.

sentences.zh: 其刑罰，殺人及盜馬者死，餘則徵物，量事決杖。

translations.literal: Their punishments: murderers and horse thieves died; the rest paid goods, deciding blows according to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Murder and horse theft were capital; lesser crimes brought fines or measured beatings.

sentences.zh: 刑人必以氈蒙頭，持石從高擊殺之。

translations.literal: When punishing a criminal they necessarily covered his head with felt and killed him by striking with a stone from high.
translations.idiomatic: Executions wrapped the head in felt and crushed it with stones dropped from height.

sentences.zh: 父兄亡後，妻後母及嫂等，與突厥俗同。

translations.literal: After father or elder brother died, one married the stepmother or sister-in-law and the like—same custom as the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Like the Turks, they took stepmothers and sisters-in-law after a father's or elder brother's death.

sentences.zh: 至于婚姻，貧不能備財物者，輒盜女將去。

translations.literal: As for marriage, those too poor to prepare goods often stole the girl and went off.
translations.idiomatic: Poor suitors who could not afford bride-price often abducted the bride.

sentences.zh: 死者亦皆埋殯。

translations.literal: The dead too were all buried.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were buried as well.

sentences.zh: 其服制，葬訖則除之。

translations.literal: Their mourning dress was removed once burial was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning garb ended when burial was complete.

sentences.zh: 性貪婪，忍於殺害。

translations.literal: By nature they were greedy and endured killing.
translations.idiomatic: They were greedy by nature and ruthless in killing.

sentences.zh: 好射獵，以肉酪為糧。

translations.literal: They loved hunting and took meat and curds as grain.
translations.idiomatic: They hunted avidly and lived on meat and curds.

sentences.zh: 亦知種田，然其北界，氣候多寒，唯得蕪菁、大麥。

translations.literal: They also knew farming, but on their northern border the climate was mostly cold and they could obtain only turnips and barley.
translations.idiomatic: They farmed too, but the northern climate yielded only turnips and barley.

sentences.zh: 故其俗貧多富少。

translations.literal: Therefore in their custom the poor were many and the rich few.
translations.idiomatic: Hence poverty was common and wealth rare.

sentences.zh: 青海周回千餘里，海內有小山。

translations.literal: Qinghai circled more than a thousand li; within the sea were small mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghai Lake spanned over a thousand li, with islets within it.

sentences.zh: 每冬冰合後，以良牝馬置此山，至來冬收之，馬皆有孕，所生得駒，號為龍種，必多駿異，世傳青海

translations.literal: Each winter after the ice closed they placed fine mares on this mountain; the next winter when they collected them the mares were all pregnant; the foals born were called dragon stock, invariably many exceptional steeds; tradition says Qinghai
translations.idiomatic: Each winter after the ice set they pastured choice mares on the islet; when collected next winter every mare was in foal; the colts, called dragon stock, were famed as exceptional mounts; tradition names them Qinghai

translations.literal: missing character jun
translations.idiomatic: text lost here: jun

sentences.zh: 〔驄〕者也。

translations.literal: supplied character cong coursers
translations.idiomatic: emended: Qinghai coursers.

sentences.zh: 土出犛牛，鳥多鸚鵡。

translations.literal: The soil produced yak; birds were many parrots.
translations.idiomatic: The land bred yaks; parrots flocked there.

sentences.zh: 大統中，夸呂再遣使獻馬及羊牛等。

translations.literal: In Datong, Kua-lu twice sent envoys presenting horses and sheep and cattle and the like.
translations.idiomatic: During Datong Kua-lu twice sent horses, sheep, and cattle as tribute.

sentences.zh: 然猶寇抄不止，緣邊多被其害。

translations.literal: Yet they still raided without cease, and the frontier suffered much harm from them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet border raids never ceased and the frontier suffered heavily.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，太祖勒大兵至姑臧，夸呂震懼，遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei, the Grand Ancestor led a great army to Guzang; Kua-lu was shaken with fear and sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Fei's second year the Grand Ancestor marched on Guzang; terrified, Kua-lu sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，夸呂又通使於齊氏。

translations.literal: That year Kua-lu also sent envoys to the Qi.
translations.idiomatic: That year he also opened relations with Qi.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史史甯覘知其還，率輕騎襲之於州西赤泉，獲其僕射乞伏觸扳、將軍翟潘密、商胡二百四十人，駝騾六百頭，雜彩絲絹以萬計。

translations.literal: Liangzhou Inspector Shi Ning, observing his return, led light cavalry to strike him west of the prefecture at Red Spring, capturing his puye Qi-fu Chu-ban, general Zhai Pan-mi, and two hundred forty Sogdian merchants, six hundred camels and mules, and more than ten thousand measures of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Shi Ning ambushed his return at Red Spring west of the prefecture, seizing puye Qi-fu Chu-ban, general Zhai Pan-mi, two hundred forty Sogdian merchants, six hundred pack animals, and vast silks.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，史寧又與突厥木汗可汗襲擊夸呂，破之，虜其妻子，大獲珍物及雜畜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, Shi Ning again with the Turk Mu-han Qaghan attacked Kua-lu, defeated him, captured his wife and children, and gained great treasures and miscellaneous livestock.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gong's second year Shi Ning and Turk Mu-han Qaghan routed Kua-lu, taking his family and great spoils.

sentences.zh: 語在《史寧傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Shi Ning."
translations.idiomatic: The account appears in the Biography of Shi Ning.

sentences.zh: 武成初，夸呂復寇涼州，刺史是云寶戰沒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wucheng, Kua-lu again raided Liangzhou; Inspector Shi Yun-bao died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wucheng Kua-lu raided Liangzhou again; Inspector Shi Yun-bao fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔賀蘭祥、宇文貴率兵討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered He-lan Xiang and Yuwen Gui to lead troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent He-lan Xiang and Yuwen Gui against him.

sentences.zh: 夸呂遣其廣定王、鐘留王拒戰，祥等破之，廣定等遁走。

translations.literal: Kua-lu sent his Prince of Guangding and Prince of Zhongliu to resist; Xiang and the others defeated them and Guangding and the others fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kua-lu sent Princes Guangding and Zhongliu; Xiang defeated them and they fled.

sentences.zh: 又攻拔其洮陽、洪和二城，置洮州以還。

translations.literal: They again attacked and took his cities of Tao-yang and Hong-he, established Tao Prefecture, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Tao-yang and Hong-he, set up Tao Prefecture, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 保定中，夸呂前後三輩遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In Baoding, Kua-lu before and after sent three missions presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoding Kua-lu sent three embassies with tribute.

sentences.zh: 天和初，其龍涸王莫昌率衆降，以其地為扶州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, his Prince of Longhu Mo-chang led the masses in surrender; his territory was made Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianhe Prince Mo-chang of Longhu surrendered; his lands became Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，復遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, he again sent envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year two he sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 建德五年，其國大亂。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiande, their state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiande the realm collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔皇太子征之，軍渡青海，至伏俟城。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered the crown prince to campaign; the army crossed Qinghai and reached Fu-hou City.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent the crown prince; the army crossed Qinghai to Fu-hou City.

sentences.zh: 夸呂遁走，虜其餘衆而還。

translations.literal: Kua-lu fled; they captured his remaining masses and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Kua-lu fled; they took his remnant people and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，又再遣奉獻。

translations.literal: The next year, they again twice sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute twice more.

sentences.zh: 宣政初，其趙王他婁屯來降。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzheng, their Prince Zhao Wang Ta-lou-tun came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xuanzheng Prince Ta-lou-tun of Zhao came over.

sentences.zh: 自是朝獻遂絕。

translations.literal: From this court presentations ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Court tribute then ended.

sentences.zh: 高昌者，車師前王之故地。

translations.literal: Gaochang was the old territory of the Former King of Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang was the former land of the Cheshi kings.

sentences.zh: 東去長安四千九百里，漢西域長史及戊己校尉，竝治於此。

translations.literal: Four thousand nine hundred li east of Chang'an; the Han Western Regions chief commandant and the Wuji colonel both administered from here.
translations.idiomatic: It lay four thousand nine hundred li east of Chang'an, where Han chief commandants and Wuji colonels had once ruled.

sentences.zh: 晉以其地為高昌郡。

translations.literal: Jin made the place Gaochang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jin organized it as Gaochang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 張軌、呂光、沮渠蒙遜據河西，皆置太守以統之。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, Lu Guang, and Juqu Mengxun holding Hexi all set grand administrators to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, Lu Guang, and Juqu Mengxun of Hexi each appointed governors.

sentences.zh: 其後有闞爽及沮渠無諱，竝自署為太守。

translations.literal: Afterward there were Kan Shuang and Juqu Wu-hui, each self-styling as grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kan Shuang and Juqu Wu-hui styled themselves governors.

sentences.zh: 無諱死，茹茹殺其弟安周，以闞伯周為高昌王。

translations.literal: When Wu-hui died, the Rouran killed his younger brother An-zhou and installed Kan Bo-zhou as king of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu-hui died the Rouran killed his brother An-zhou and made Kan Bo-zhou king of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 高昌之稱王，自此始也。

translations.literal: Gaochang's styling itself king began from this.
translations.idiomatic: This was when Gaochang first called itself a kingdom.

sentences.zh: 伯周之從子首歸，為高車所滅。

translations.literal: Bo-zhou's younger clansman Shou-gui was destroyed by the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: Bo-zhou's clansman Shou-gui was overthrown by the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 次有張孟明、馬儒相繼王之，竝為國人所害。

translations.literal: Next Zhang Mengming and Ma Ru succeeded one another as kings, both killed by their countrymen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mengming and Ma Ru ruled in turn, both slain by their own people.

sentences.zh: 乃更推立麴嘉為王。

translations.literal: They then again pushed forward and established Qu Jia as king.
translations.idiomatic: The people then elevated Qu Jia as king.

sentences.zh: 嘉字靈鳳，金城榆中人，本為儒右長史。

translations.literal: Jia, styled Ling-feng, was a man of Yuzhong in Jincheng, originally right chief clerk of the Confucian faction.
translations.idiomatic: Jia, courtesy name Ling-feng, came from Yuzhong in Jincheng and had been chief clerk on the right.

sentences.zh: 魏太和末立。

translations.literal: He was installed at the end of Taihe of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He took the throne at the end of Wei Taihe.

sentences.zh: 嘉死，子

translations.literal: When Jia died, his son
translations.idiomatic: When Jia died, his son

translations.literal: missing character shu
translations.idiomatic: text lost: shu

sentences.zh: 〔堅〕立。

translations.literal: supplied character jian succeeded to the throne
translations.idiomatic: emended: Jian succeeded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 其地東西三百里，南北五百里。

translations.literal: Its territory was three hundred li east to west and five hundred li north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The realm measured three hundred li east-west and five hundred li north-south.

sentences.zh: 國內總有城一十六。

translations.literal: Within the state there were altogether sixteen walled cities.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen walled towns lay within the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 官有令尹一人，比中夏相國；

translations.literal: In office there was one lingyin, comparable to the chancellor of the Central States;
translations.idiomatic: A single lingyin served as chancellor by Chinese standards;

sentences.zh: 次有公二人，皆其王子也，一為交河公，一為田地公；

translations.literal: next two dukes, both princes of the royal house—one Duke of Jiaohe, one Duke of Tiandi;
translations.idiomatic: below him two royal dukes—the Duke of Jiaohe and the Duke of Tiandi;

sentences.zh: 次有左右衛；

translations.literal: next left and right guards;
translations.idiomatic: then left and right guards;

sentences.zh: 次有八長史，曰吏部、祠部、庫部、倉部、主客、禮部、民部、兵部等長史也；

translations.literal: next eight chief clerks: Personnel, Sacrifices, Treasury, Granary, Foreign Guests, Rites, People, and War chief clerks;
translations.idiomatic: eight chief clerks for personnel, rites, treasury, granary, foreign guests, rites, people, and war;

sentences.zh: 次有建武、威遠、陵江、殿中、伏波等將軍；

translations.literal: next generals Jianwu, Weiyuan, Lingjiang, Dianzhong, Fubo, and the like;
translations.idiomatic: generals such as Jianwu, Weiyuan, Lingjiang, Dianzhong, and Fubo;

sentences.zh: 次有八司馬，長史之副也；

translations.literal: next eight majors, deputies to the chief clerks;
translations.idiomatic: eight majors as deputies to the chief clerks;

sentences.zh: 次有侍郎、校書郎、主簿、從事，階位相次，分掌諸事；

translations.literal: next attendant gentlemen, collation clerks, recorders, and clerks, ranks in sequence, each administering affairs;
translations.idiomatic: then attendants, collation clerks, recorders, and clerks in descending rank;

sentences.zh: 次有省事，專掌導引。

translations.literal: next attendants-in-chief who exclusively directed protocol.
translations.idiomatic: finally protocol officers who guided ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其大事決之於王，小事則世子及二公隨狀斷決。

translations.literal: Great affairs were decided by the king; small affairs were adjudicated case by case by the heir and the two dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The king decided great matters; the heir and two dukes handled lesser cases.

sentences.zh: 平章錄記，事訖卽除。

translations.literal: They reviewed and recorded; when the matter ended the post was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Records were kept only for the case at hand, then struck.

sentences.zh: 籍書之外，無久掌文桉。

translations.literal: Apart from registry books there were no long-kept document files.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond registries no archives were retained.

sentences.zh: 官人雖有列位，竝無曹府，唯每旦集於牙門評議衆事。

translations.literal: Officials though having ranked posts all had no bureaus; they only gathered each dawn at the gate to discuss the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had titles but no offices, meeting each dawn at the gate to debate business.

sentences.zh: 諸城各有戶曹、水曹、田曹。

translations.literal: Each city had household, water, and field bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Each town had household, water, and field officers.

sentences.zh: 每城遣司馬、侍郎相監檢校，名為城令。

translations.literal: Each city sent a major and attendant gentleman to supervise and inspect, styled city magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Each city sent a major and attendant to inspect, called city magistrate.

sentences.zh: 服飾，丈夫從胡法，婦人略同華夏。

translations.literal: Dress: husbands followed Hu custom; women were much like the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Men dressed in Hu fashion; women dressed much like Chinese women.

sentences.zh: 兵器有弓箭刀楯甲矟。

translations.literal: Weapons included bow, arrow, knife, shield, armor, and spear.
translations.idiomatic: Arms were bow, arrow, sword, shield, armor, and spear.

sentences.zh: 文字亦同華夏，兼用胡書。

translations.literal: Writing also matched the Central States, while also using Hu script.
translations.idiomatic: They wrote in Chinese script and also in Hu writing.

sentences.zh: 有《毛詩》、《論語》、《孝經》，置學官弟子，以相教授。

translations.literal: They had the Mao Odes, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, set up school officers and disciples to teach one another.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained schools teaching the Odes, Analects, and Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 雖習讀之，而皆為胡語。

translations.literal: Although they practiced reading, all were in Hu speech.
translations.idiomatic: Students read the classics, yet instruction was in Hu tongue.

sentences.zh: 賦稅則計輸銀錢，無者輸麻布。

translations.literal: For levies they calculated payment in silver cash; those without paid hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were reckoned in silver; the poor paid in hemp cloth.

sentences.zh: 其刑法、風俗、婚姻、喪葬，與華夏小異而大同。

translations.literal: Penal code, customs, marriage, and burial were slightly different from the Central States yet broadly the same.
translations.idiomatic: Law, custom, marriage, and burial differed slightly from China yet broadly matched it.

sentences.zh: 地多石磧，氣候溫暖，穀麥再熟，宜蠶，多五果。

translations.literal: The land was much stony desert; the climate warm; grain and wheat ripened twice; silkworms thrived; many five fruits.
translations.idiomatic: Stony soil and warm climate yielded double harvests, thriving silkworms, and abundant fruit.

sentences.zh: 有草曰羊剌，其上生蜜焉。

translations.literal: There was a grass called yang-la; honey grew upon it.
translations.idiomatic: A grass called yang-la bore honey on its stalks.

sentences.zh: 自嘉以來，世修蕃職於魏。

translations.literal: From Jia onward they generation after generation performed frontier duty to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jia's day they had served Wei as frontier vassals.

sentences.zh: 大統十四年，詔以其世子玄喜為王。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Datong, an edict made his heir Xuan-xi king.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong fourteen his heir Xuan-xi was enfeoffed as king.

sentences.zh: 恭帝二年，又以其田地公茂嗣位。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong, his Duke of Tiandi Mao succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gong's second year Duke Mao of Tiandi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，其王遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng, the king sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng's first year the king sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 保定初，又遣使來貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he again sent envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoding tribute came again.

sentences.zh: 自燉煌向其國，多沙磧，道里不可准記，唯以人畜骸骨及駝馬糞為驗，又有魍魎怪異。

translations.literal: From Dunhuang toward their state was much sandy desert; the route could not be measured by li; only human and animal bones and camel and horse dung served as markers, and there were also goblins and strange things.
translations.idiomatic: The road from Dunhuang was trackless desert marked only by bones and dung, haunted by omens and monsters.

sentences.zh: 故商旅來往，多取伊吾路云。

translations.literal: Therefore merchants traveling back and forth mostly took the Yiwu route.
translations.idiomatic: Traders therefore usually went by the Yiwu road.

sentences.zh: 鄯善，古樓蘭國也。

translations.literal: Shanshan was the old state of Loulan.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshan was ancient Loulan.

sentences.zh: 東去長安五千里。

translations.literal: Five thousand li east of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: It lay five thousand li east of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 所治城方一里。

translations.literal: The seat city was one li square.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital measured one li square.

sentences.zh: 地多沙鹵，少水草。

translations.literal: The land was much salty sand and little water or grass.
translations.idiomatic: Saline sands dominated; water and pasture were scarce.

sentences.zh: 北卽白龍堆路。

translations.literal: Northward lay the road of the White Dragon Mounds.
translations.idiomatic: To the north ran the White Dragon Mounds route.

sentences.zh: 魏太武時，為沮渠安周所攻，其王西奔且末。

translations.literal: In the era of Emperor Taiwu of Wei, it was attacked by Juqu An-zhou; its king fled west to Qiemo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu's day saw Juqu An-zhou attack it; the king fled west to Qiemo.

sentences.zh: 西北有流沙數百里，夏日有熱風，為行旅之患。

translations.literal: Northwest were drifting sands several hundred li; in summer there were hot winds, a trouble for travelers.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of li northwest lay drifting sands where summer brought scorching winds.

sentences.zh: 風之欲至，唯老駝知之，卽鳴而聚立，埋其口鼻於沙中。

translations.literal: When the wind was about to come, only old camels knew it; they then cried and gathered standing, burying muzzles in the sand.
translations.idiomatic: Old camels alone sensed the coming wind, crying and burying their muzzles in sand.

sentences.zh: 人每以為候，亦卽將氈擁蔽鼻口。

translations.literal: People each took this as a sign and also immediately used felt to cover and shield nose and mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers took the camels' warning and masked nose and mouth with felt.

sentences.zh: 其風迅駛，斯須過盡。

translations.literal: The wind ran swift and in an instant passed entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The gale struck swiftly and passed in moments.

sentences.zh: 若不防者，必至危斃。

translations.literal: If one did not guard against it, one necessarily reached danger and death.
translations.idiomatic: Without such precautions travelers perished.

sentences.zh: 大統八年，其〔王〕兄鄯米率衆內附。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Datong, his supplied wang brother Shan-mi led the masses in internal submission.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong eight the king's brother Shan-mi submitted with his people.

sentences.zh: 焉耆國在白山之南七十里，東去長安五千八百里。

translations.literal: The state of Karasahr lay seventy li south of White Mountain, five thousand eight hundred li east of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Karasahr stood seventy li south of White Mountain, five thousand eight hundred li from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 其王姓龍，卽前涼張軌所

translations.literal: Its king surnamed Long—that is, the descendant of Long Xi whom Former Liang Zhang Gui
translations.idiomatic: Its kings bore the surname Long, descendants of Long Xi whom Former Liang's Zhang Gui

translations.literal: enfeoffed
translations.idiomatic: had enfeoffed

sentences.zh: 〔討〕龍熙之胤。

translations.literal: supplied character tao Long Xi's descendant.
translations.idiomatic: emended: and whom Zhang Gui had enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 所治城方二里。

translations.literal: The seat city was two li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was two li square.

sentences.zh: 部內凡有九城。

translations.literal: Within the territory were nine cities in all.
translations.idiomatic: Nine towns lay within the realm.

sentences.zh: 國小民貧，無綱紀法令。

translations.literal: The state was small and the people poor, without statutes or ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Small and poor, it lacked codified law.

sentences.zh: 兵有弓刀甲矟。

translations.literal: Arms included bow, knife, armor, and spear.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons were bow, knife, armor, and spear.

sentences.zh: 婚姻略同華夏。

translations.literal: Marriage was broadly like the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage customs resembled China's.

sentences.zh: 死亡者皆焚而後葬，其服制滿七日則除之。

translations.literal: The dead were all burned and afterward buried; mourning dress was removed after seven full days.
translations.idiomatic: The dead were cremated then buried; mourning ended after seven days.

sentences.zh: 丈夫竝剪發以為首飾。

translations.literal: Husbands all cut their hair to make head ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Men cropped their hair for ornament.

sentences.zh: 文字與婆羅門同。

translations.literal: Writing was the same as Brahman script.
translations.idiomatic: Their script matched Brahman writing.

sentences.zh: 俗事天神，竝崇信佛法。

translations.literal: In custom they served the Heaven God and together honored Buddhist law.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped Heaven and revered Buddhism alike.

sentences.zh: 尤重二月八日、四月八日。

translations.literal: They especially honored the eighth day of the second month and the eighth day of the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: The second-month eighth day and fourth-month eighth day were especially sacred.

sentences.zh: 是日也，其國咸依釋教，齋戒行道焉。

translations.literal: On those days the whole state followed Buddhist teaching, fasting and practicing the Way.
translations.idiomatic: On those days the whole realm fasted and observed Buddhist rites.

sentences.zh: 氣候寒，土田良沃。

translations.literal: The climate was cold; fields and soil were fertile and rich.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was cold but the soil fertile.

sentences.zh: 榖有稻粟菽麥。

translations.literal: Grains included rice, millet, beans, and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: They grew rice, millet, beans, and wheat.

sentences.zh: 畜有駝馬牛羊。

translations.literal: Livestock included camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Herds held camels, horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 養蠶不以為絲，唯充綿纊。

translations.literal: They raised silkworms but did not make them into silk, only filling cotton wadding.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworms were raised for cotton wadding, not silk thread.

sentences.zh: 俗尚蒲桃酒，兼愛音樂。

translations.literal: The custom prized grape wine and also loved music.
translations.idiomatic: They prized grape wine and loved music.

sentences.zh: 南去海十餘里，有魚鹽蒲葦之饒。

translations.literal: Southward ten-odd li from the sea were rich fish, salt, reeds, and rushes.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-odd li south of the sea lay rich fisheries, salt, and reeds.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，其王遣使獻名馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, the king sent envoys presenting famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding four the king sent famed horses.

sentences.zh: 龜茲國在白山之南一百七十里，東去長安六千七百里。

translations.literal: The state of Kucha lay one hundred seventy li south of White Mountain, six thousand seven hundred li east of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha lay one hundred seventy li south of White Mountain, six thousand seven hundred li from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 其王姓白，卽後涼呂光所立白震之後。

translations.literal: Its king surnamed Bai—that is, the descendant of Bai Zhen whom Later Liang Lu Guang installed.
translations.idiomatic: Kings surnamed Bai descended from Bai Zhen, whom Later Liang's Lu Guang had installed.

sentences.zh: 所治城方五六里。

translations.literal: The seat city was five or six li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured five or six li square.

sentences.zh: 其刑法，殺人者死，劫賊則斷其一臂，並刖一足。

translations.literal: Their penal code: murderers died; robbers had one arm cut off and one foot amputated.
translations.idiomatic: Murder was capital; robbers lost an arm and a foot.

sentences.zh: 賦稅，准地征租，無田者則稅銀錢。

translations.literal: Levies followed land rent by territory; those without fields paid silver cash.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were land rents; the landless paid silver.

sentences.zh: 婚姻、喪葬、風俗、物產與焉支略同。

translations.literal: Marriage, burial, customs, and products were broadly the same as Karasahr.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage, burial, customs, and products resembled Karasahr's.

sentences.zh: 唯氣候少溫為異。

translations.literal: Only the climate was somewhat warmer as the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Only the climate ran somewhat warmer.

sentences.zh: 又出細氈、麖皮、氍毺、鐃

translations.literal: They also produced fine felt, elk hide, carpets, cymbals
translations.idiomatic: They also exported fine felt, elk hide, carpets, and cymbals,

translations.literal: many
translations.idiomatic: many

sentences.zh: 〔沙〕、鹽綠、雌黃、胡粉及良馬、封牛等。

translations.literal: supplied sha sand green, orpiment, Hu powder, and fine horses, zebu cattle, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: emended: sand, mineral green, orpiment, cosmetic powder, fine horses, and zebu cattle.

sentences.zh: 東有輪臺，卽漢貳師將軍李廣利所屠。

translations.literal: East was Luntai—that which Han General Li Guangli had slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: East lay Luntai, sacked by Han general Li Guangli.

sentences.zh: 其南三百里有大水東流，號計戍水，卽黃河也。

translations.literal: Three hundred li south was a great river flowing east, called the Jigu River—that is, the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li south a great river, the Jigu or Yellow River, flowed east.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，其王遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, the king sent envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding's first year the king sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 于闐國在蔥嶺之北二百餘里，東去長安七千七百里。

translations.literal: The state of Khotan lay more than two hundred li north of the Onion Range, seven thousand seven hundred li east of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan stood north of the Onion Range, seven thousand seven hundred li from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 所治城方八九里。

translations.literal: The seat city was eight or nine li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital measured eight or nine li square.

sentences.zh: 部內有大城五，小城數十。

translations.literal: Within the territory were five great cities and several tens of small cities.
translations.idiomatic: Five great cities and dozens of lesser towns lay within the realm.

sentences.zh: 其刑法，殺人者死，餘罪各隨輕重懲罰之。

translations.literal: Their penal code: murderers died; remaining crimes were each punished according to severity.
translations.idiomatic: Murder was capital; lesser crimes brought scaled punishments.

sentences.zh: 自外風俗物產與龜茲略同。

translations.literal: Apart from this, customs and products were broadly the same as Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise customs and products matched Kucha's.

sentences.zh: 俗重佛法，寺塔僧尼甚衆。

translations.literal: The custom heavily honored Buddhist law; temples, pagodas, monks, and nuns were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism flourished with countless temples, pagodas, monks, and nuns.

sentences.zh: 王尤信向，每設齋日，必親自灑掃饋食焉。

translations.literal: The king especially believed; each fast day he personally sprinkled and swept and offered food.
translations.idiomatic: The king was devout, personally sweeping and feeding monks on fast days.

sentences.zh: 城南五十里有贊摩寺，卽昔羅漢比丘比盧旃為其王造覆盆浮圖之所。

translations.literal: Fifty li south of the city was Zanmo Temple—that where in the past the arhat monk Piluzhan built a bowl-cover stupa for his king.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li south stood Zanmo Temple, where the arhat Piluzhan had built a bowl-shaped stupa for the king.

sentences.zh: 石上有辟支佛趺處，雙跡猶存。

translations.literal: On the stone was the seat-mark of a pratyekabuddha; the twin footprints still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Stone there still bore a pratyekabuddha's footprints.

sentences.zh: 自高昌以西，諸國人等多深目高

translations.literal: West of Gaochang, the people of the various states were mostly deep-eyed and high
translations.idiomatic: West of Gaochang peoples were mostly deep-eyed and high-

sentences.zh: （昌以東）

translations.literal: east of Chang
translations.idiomatic: nosed east of Chang—

sentences.zh: 〔鼻，唯〕此一國，貌不甚胡，頗類華夏。

translations.literal: supplied bi; only this one state, the appearance not very Hu, quite resembling the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: emended: nosed; Khotan alone looked less foreign and more Chinese.

sentences.zh: 城東二十里有大水北流，號樹枝水，卽黃河也。

translations.literal: Twenty li east of the city was a great river flowing north, called the Branch River—that is, the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li east the Branch River, a Yellow River tributary, flowed north.

sentences.zh: 城西十五里亦有大水，名達利水，與樹枝俱北流，同會於計戍。

translations.literal: Fifteen li west of the city was also a great river, named Dali River; with the Branch it flowed north together and met at Jigu.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen li west the Dali River joined the Branch northward at Jigu.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，其王遣使獻名馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, the king sent envoys presenting famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande three the king sent famed horses.

sentences.zh: 囐噠國，大月氐之種類，在于闐之西，東去長安一萬百里。

translations.literal: The state of the Hephtalites was a branch of the Great Yuezhi, west of Khotan, ten thousand li east of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Hephtalites were a Yuezhi branch west of Khotan, ten thousand li from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 其王治拔底延城，蓋王舍城也。

translations.literal: Their king ruled from Badiyan City—probably Rajagriha.
translations.idiomatic: Their king ruled Badiyan City, perhaps ancient Rajagriha.

sentences.zh: 其城方十餘里。

translations.literal: The city was more than ten li square.
translations.idiomatic: The capital exceeded ten li square.

sentences.zh: 刑法、風俗，與突厥略同。

translations.literal: Penal code and customs were broadly the same as the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Law and custom resembled the Turks'.

sentences.zh: 其俗又兄弟共娶一妻。

translations.literal: In their custom brothers also shared marrying one wife.
translations.idiomatic: Custom also allowed brothers to share one wife.

sentences.zh: 夫無兄弟者，其妻戴一角帽；

translations.literal: For a man without brothers, his wife wore a hat with one horn;
translations.idiomatic: A wife whose husband had no brothers wore a one-horned cap;

sentences.zh: 若有兄弟者，依其多少之數，更加帽角焉。

translations.literal: if there were brothers, according to their number additional hat horns were added.
translations.idiomatic: each brother added another horn to her cap.

sentences.zh: 其人兇悍，能戰鬬。

translations.literal: The people were fierce and could fight.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce warriors.

sentences.zh: 于闐、安息等大小二十餘國，皆役屬之。

translations.literal: Khotan, Parthia, and more than twenty states great and small were all made to serve and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan, Parthia, and twenty-odd lesser states all served them.

sentences.zh: 大統十二年，遣使獻其方物。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Datong, they sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong twelve they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，明帝二年，竝遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei and the second year of Emperor Ming, they both sent envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Fei's second year and Emperor Ming's second year they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 後為突厥所破，部落分散，職貢遂絕。

translations.literal: Afterward they were broken by the Turks; the tribes scattered and frontier tribute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks shattered them; tribes scattered and tribute ended.

sentences.zh: 粟特國在蔥嶺之西，蓋古之庵蔡，一名溫那沙。

translations.literal: The state of Sogdia lay west of the Onion Range; it was probably ancient Ancai, also called Wuna-sha.
translations.idiomatic: Sogdia west of the Onion Range was ancient Ancai, also Wuna-sha.

sentences.zh: 治于大澤，在康居西北。

translations.literal: They ruled from a great marsh, northwest of Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Their seat lay in a great marsh northwest of Kangju.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，其王遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, the king sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding four the king sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 安息國在蔥嶺之西，治蔚搜城。

translations.literal: The state of Parthia lay west of the Onion Range, ruling from Weisou City.
translations.idiomatic: Parthia west of the Onion Range ruled from Weisou City.

sentences.zh: 北與康居、西與波斯相接，東去長安一萬七百五十里。

translations.literal: North it bordered Kangju, west it joined Persia, ten thousand seven hundred fifty li east of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Kangju north, Persia west, and lay ten thousand seven hundred fifty li from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，其王遣使來獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, the king sent envoys presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhe two the king sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 波斯國，大月氐之別種，治蘇利城，古條支國也。

translations.literal: The state of Persia was a separate branch of the Great Yuezhi, ruling from Suli City—the old state of Tiao-zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Persia was a Yuezhi offshoot ruling Suli City, ancient Tiao-zhi.

sentences.zh: 東去長安一萬五千三百里。

translations.literal: Fifteen thousand three hundred li east of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: It stood fifteen thousand three hundred li east of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 城方十餘里，戶十餘萬。

translations.literal: The city was more than ten li square; households numbered more than one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The capital exceeded ten li square and held over one hundred thousand households.

sentences.zh: 王姓波斯氐。

translations.literal: The king surnamed Bo-si Di.
translations.idiomatic: Kings bore the surname Bo-si Di.

sentences.zh: 坐金羊床，戴金花冠，衣錦袍、織成帔，皆飾以珍珠寶物。

translations.literal: He sat on a golden sheep couch, wore a golden-flower crown, brocade robe and woven mantle, all ornamented with pearls and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: He sat on a golden sheep throne, crowned with gold flowers, robed in brocade and woven mantles studded with pearls.

sentences.zh: 其俗：丈夫剪發，戴白皮帽，貫頭衫，兩廂近下開之，並有巾帔，緣以織成；

translations.literal: Their custom: husbands cut their hair, wore white felt caps, collarless shirts open at both sides near the bottom, and also had turbans and scarfs edged with weaving;
translations.idiomatic: Men cropped their hair, wore white felt caps and collarless shirts open at the sides, with woven-edged turbans;

sentences.zh: 婦女服大衫，披大帔，其發前為髻，後被之，飾以金銀華，仍貫五色珠，絡之於膊。

translations.literal: women wore great robes and draped great mantles; their hair was done in a bun in front and draped behind, ornamented with gold and silver splendor, still threading five-colored pearls and netting them on the arms.
translations.idiomatic: women wore great robes and mantles, hair bound forward and draped back, adorned with gold, silver, and strings of five-colored pearls on the arms.

sentences.zh: 王於其國內別有小牙十餘所，猶中國之離宮也，每年四月出遊處之，十月乃還。

translations.literal: Within his state the king separately had more than ten lesser camps, like the detached palaces of the Central States; each year in the fourth month he went out to tour and dwell at them, returning only in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Like Chinese detached palaces he kept a dozen lesser camps, touring them each fourth month and returning in the tenth.

sentences.zh: 王卽位以後，擇諸子內賢者，密書其名，封之於庫，諸子及大臣皆莫之知也。

translations.literal: After the king took the throne he chose the worthy among his sons within, secretly wrote the name, sealed it in the treasury; sons and great ministers all did not know.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he secretly sealed the name of his worthiest son in the treasury, unknown even to princes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 王死，乃衆共發書視之，其封內有名者，卽立以為王，餘子各出就邊任。

translations.literal: When the king died, all together opened the letter and viewed it; whoever was named within the seal was thereupon installed as king; the remaining sons each went out to border posts.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the seal was opened and the named son enthroned; other sons took border commands.

sentences.zh: 兄弟更不相見也。

translations.literal: Brothers moreover did not see one another again.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers thereafter never met.

sentences.zh: 國人號王曰翳囋，妃曰防步率，王之諸子曰殺野。

translations.literal: The people styled the king Yizhe, the consort Fangbu-shuai, and the king's sons Shaye.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects called the king Yizhe, his consort Fangbu-shuai, and royal sons Shaye.

sentences.zh: 大官有摸胡壇，掌國內獄訟；

translations.literal: Great officers included Mo-hu-tan, administering domestic lawsuits;
translations.idiomatic: Chief officers included Mo-hu-tan for domestic suits;

sentences.zh: 泥忽汗，掌庫藏關禁；

translations.literal: Ni-hu-han, administering treasury stores and passes;
translations.idiomatic: Ni-hu-han for treasury and passes;

sentences.zh: 地卑勃，掌文書及衆務。

translations.literal: Di-bei-bo, administering documents and the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Di-bei-bo for documents and general affairs.

sentences.zh: 次有遏羅訶地，掌王之內事；

translations.literal: Next were E-luo-he-di, administering the king's inner affairs;
translations.idiomatic: E-luo-he-di managed the royal household;

sentences.zh: 薩波勃，掌四方兵馬。

translations.literal: Sa-bo-bo, administering troops and horses on the four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Sa-bo-bo commanded armies on all sides.

sentences.zh: 其下皆有屬官，分統其事。

translations.literal: Below them all were subordinate officials, each administering affairs in division.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officials beneath them divided the duties.

sentences.zh: 兵器有甲矟圓排劍弩弓箭。

translations.literal: Weapons included armor, spear, round shield, sword, crossbow, bow, and arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Arms included armor, spear, round shield, sword, crossbow, bow, and arrow.

sentences.zh: 戰竝乘象，每象百人隨之。

translations.literal: In battle they all rode elephants; each elephant had one hundred men following it.
translations.idiomatic: They fought from elephants, each beast attended by one hundred men.

sentences.zh: 其刑法：重罪懸諸竿上，射而殺之；
