translations.literal: Their penal code: for heavy crimes one was suspended on a pole and shot to death;
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes meant suspension on a pole and death by arrows;

sentences.zh: 次則繋獄，新王立乃釋之；

translations.literal: next one was imprisoned; when the new king was installed one was released;
translations.idiomatic: lesser felonies brought prison until a new king's accession;

sentences.zh: 輕罪則劓、刖若髡，或翦半須，及繋排於項上，以為恥辱；

translations.literal: light crimes brought cutting off the nose, amputation of feet, or shaving the head, or cutting half the beard, or fastening a board on the neck as shame;
translations.idiomatic: minor crimes brought nose-cutting, amputation, tonsure, half-beard clipping, or a shame-board at the neck;

sentences.zh: 犯彊盜者，禁之終身；

translations.literal: those who committed violent robbery were confined for life;
translations.idiomatic: violent robbers were imprisoned for life;

sentences.zh: 姦貴人妻者，男子流，婦人割其耳鼻。

translations.literal: those who committed adultery with a nobleman's wife—the man was exiled, the woman's ears and nose were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: adultery with a nobleman's wife exiled the man and mutilated the woman.

sentences.zh: 賦稅則准地輸銀錢。

translations.literal: Levies followed land in paying silver cash.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were land rents paid in silver.

sentences.zh: 俗事火祆神。

translations.literal: In custom they served the fire god of the Zoroastrian faith.
translations.idiomatic: They worshipped the Zoroastrian fire god.

sentences.zh: 婚合亦不擇尊卑，諸夷之中，最為醜穢矣。

translations.literal: Marriage unions also did not choose between noble and base; among all the barbarians they were the most ugly and filthy.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage ignored rank; among barbarians they were deemed the most debased.

sentences.zh: 民女年十歲以上有姿貌者，王收養之，有功勳人，卽以分賜。

translations.literal: Common girls above ten years with beauty were collected by the king; when there were meritorious men, they were then distributed and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The king took comely girls over ten; meritorious men received them as rewards.

sentences.zh: 死者多棄屍於山，一月治服。

translations.literal: Most of the dead were abandoned as corpses on mountains; mourning dress was settled in one month.
translations.idiomatic: Corpses were often left on mountains; mourning lasted one month.

sentences.zh: 城外有人別居，唯知喪葬之事，號為不淨人。

translations.literal: Outside the city others dwelt separately, knowing only funeral affairs, styled Unclean People.
translations.idiomatic: Outcasts beyond the walls handled funerals alone, called Unclean People.

sentences.zh: 若入城市，搖鈴自別。

translations.literal: If they entered the city, they rang a bell to distinguish themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the city they rang bells to warn others.

sentences.zh: 以六月為歲首，尤重七月七日、十二月一日。

translations.literal: They took the sixth month as year beginning and especially honored the seventh day of the seventh month and the first day of the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: Their year began in the sixth month; the seventh-month seventh day and twelfth-month first day were especially sacred.

sentences.zh: 其日，民庶以上，各相命召，設會作樂，以極歡娛。

translations.literal: On those days the common people upward each summoned one another, set meetings and made music, to the utmost of joy and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: On those days all ranks feasted and made music to excess.

sentences.zh: 又以每年正月二十日，各祭其先死者。

translations.literal: Also on the twentieth day of the first month each year they sacrificed to their dead forebears.
translations.idiomatic: Each first-month twentieth day they sacrificed to ancestors.

sentences.zh: 氣候暑熱，家自藏冰。

translations.literal: The climate was hot; families each stored ice.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was torrid; households stored ice.

sentences.zh: 地多沙磧，引水溉灌。

translations.literal: The land was much sandy desert; they led water to irrigate and pour.
translations.idiomatic: Sandy soil required irrigation.

sentences.zh: 其五穀及禽獸等，與中夏略同，唯無稻及黍秫。

translations.literal: Their five grains and birds and beasts and the like were broadly the same as the Central States; only they lacked rice and broomcorn millet.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and livestock resembled China's save for rice and broomcorn millet.

sentences.zh: 土出名馬及駝，富室至有數千頭者。

translations.literal: The soil produced famous horses and camels; wealthy households reached several thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: The land bred famed horses and camels; rich houses owned thousands.

sentences.zh: 又出白象、師子、大鳥卵、珍珠、離珠、頗黎、珊瑚、琥珀、瑠璃、馬瑙、水晶、瑟瑟、金、銀、鍮石、金剛、火齊、鑌鐵、銅、錫、朱沙、水銀、綾、錦、白疊、毼、氍毹、毾㲪、赤麞皮，及薰六、鬱金、蘇合、青木等香，胡椒、蓽撥、石蜜、千

translations.literal: They also produced white elephants, lions, great bird eggs, pearls, li pearls, glass, coral, amber, lapis, agate, crystal, sese, gold, silver, brass, diamond, fire-glass, bin iron, copper, tin, cinnabar, mercury, damask, brocade, white layered cloth, felt, carpets, felt rugs, red elk hide, and aromatics such as xunliu, tulip, storax, eaglewood, and also pepper, long pepper, rock honey, thousand
translations.idiomatic: They exported white elephants, lions, ostrich eggs, pearls, glass, coral, amber, lapis, agate, crystal, gold, silver, metals, gems, silks, felts, aromatics, pepper, rock honey, thousand-

translations.idiomatic: ox

sentences.zh: 〔年〕棗、香附子、訶棃勒、無食子、鹽綠、雌黃等物。

translations.literal: supplied nian jujubes, cyperus, myrobalan, gallnuts, mineral green, orpiment, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: emended: year jujubes, cyperus, myrobalan, gallnuts, mineral green, orpiment, and more.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，其王遣使來獻方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei, the king sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Fei's second year the king sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：四夷之為中國患也久矣，而北狄尤甚焉。

translations.literal: The historian says: The four barbarians' becoming a trouble to the Central States is of long standing, and the northern Di especially so.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Border peoples have long troubled China, northern Di most of all.

sentences.zh: 昔嚴尤、班固咸以周及秦漢未有得其上策，雖通賢之宏議，而史臣嘗以為疑。

translations.literal: In the past Yan You and Ban Gu both held that from Zhou through Qin and Han none had obtained the superior stratagem; though there were penetrating worthies' grand designs, the historian has often held this in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Yan You and Ban Gu claimed Zhou through Han never found the right policy; later historians doubted them.

sentences.zh: 夫步驟之來，綿自今古；

translations.literal: The coming of steppe ways stretches from present to antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: Steppe power is no new phenomenon;

sentences.zh: 澆淳之變，無隔華戎。

translations.literal: the change of shallow and pure knows no barrier between Chinese and barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: decay and renewal cross every frontier.

sentences.zh: 是以反道德，棄仁義，淩

translations.literal: Therefore turning against the Way and Virtue, abandoning benevolence and righteousness, the wind of
translations.idiomatic: They spurned virtue and benevolence, and the wind of

translations.idiomatic: missing character

sentences.zh: 〔朁〕之風歲廣；

translations.literal: supplied chan insolence grew year by year;
translations.idiomatic: emended: insolence spread yearly;

sentences.zh: 至涇陽，入北地，充斥之釁日深。

translations.literal: reaching Jingyang, entering Beidi—the sign of filling and overflowing grew daily deeper.
translations.idiomatic: raids reached Jingyang and Beidi ever more often.

sentences.zh: 爰自金行，逮乎水運，戎夏離錯，風俗混幷。

translations.literal: From the Metal Phase down through the Water Phase, Rong and Xia parted and mixed, customs merging.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin through Sui, barbarian and Chinese realms intertwined.

sentences.zh: 夷裔之情偽，中國畢知之矣；

translations.literal: Barbarian feelings and falsity—the Central States knew them all completely;
translations.idiomatic: China knew every barbarian trick;

sentences.zh: 中國之得失，夷裔備聞之矣。

translations.literal: the Central States' gains and losses—the barbarians heard them all completely too.
translations.idiomatic: barbarians heard every Chinese weakness too.

sentences.zh: 若乃不與約誓，不就攻伐，來而禦之，去而守之；

translations.literal: If one does not make covenants with them, does not go to attack them, comes then defends against them, goes then guards against them—
translations.idiomatic: Without treaties or punitive campaigns, only reactive defense—

sentences.zh: 夫然則敵有餘力，我無寧歲，將士疲於奔命，疆埸苦其交侵。

translations.literal: then the enemy has surplus strength, we have no peaceful years; officers and soldiers weary at urgent orders, the frontier suffers from their mutual raids.
translations.idiomatic: the enemy keeps strength, we know no peace, soldiers exhaust themselves, and borders bleed.

sentences.zh: 欲使偃伯靈台，

translations.literal: Wishing to make the Martial King's terrace idle
translations.idiomatic: To idle the Martial King's terrace

translations.literal: missing character ou
translations.idiomatic: missing character

sentences.zh: 〔驅〕世仁壽，其可得乎。

translations.literal: supplied qu and drive the age to benevolent longevity—how could that be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: emended: and drive the age to benevolent longevity—was that possible?

sentences.zh: 是知秩宗之雅旨，護軍之誠說，實有會於當時，而未允於後代也。

translations.literal: From this one knows the elegant aim of the Minister of Rites and the sincere discourse of the Protector of the Army did meet the time, yet were not granted to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Rites ministers and army protectors spoke truth for their day, yet their counsel failed later ages.

sentences.zh: 然則《易》稱「見幾而作」，《傳》云「相時而動」。

translations.literal: Yet then the Changes says "seeing the subtle then acting," the Documents says "observing the time then moving."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Changes urges acting on subtle signs, the Documents on moving with the times.

sentences.zh: 夫時者，得失之所繋；

translations.literal: Time is what gain and loss are tied to;
translations.idiomatic: Timing binds gain and loss;

sentences.zh: 幾者，吉凶之所由。

translations.literal: the subtle is what fortune and calamity proceed from.
translations.idiomatic: subtle signs foretell fortune and ruin.

sentences.zh: 況乎諸夏之朝，治亂之運代有；

translations.literal: How much more the courts of the various Xia—fortunes of order and disorder each had their generations;
translations.idiomatic: Chinese dynasties rose and fell in turn;

sentences.zh: 戎狄之地，彊弱之勢無恆。

translations.literal: the lands of the Rong and Di—trends of strong and weak had no constancy.
translations.idiomatic: barbarian power waxed and waned without rule.

sentences.zh: 若使臣畜之與羈縻，和親之與征伐，因其時而制變，觀其幾而立權，則舉無遺策，謀多上算，獸心之虜，革面匪難，沙幕之北，雲撤何遠。

translations.literal: If subject-and-tenant versus loose tethering, peace marriage versus punitive campaign, were made to change with the time and authority set by observing the subtle, then in action no stratagem would be left behind and in counsel mostly superior reckoning; barbarian hearts could change their faces without difficulty, and north of the sand sea the clouds would withdraw—how far?
translations.idiomatic: Vassalage, loose tether, marriage, or war—timed rightly—would leave no stratagem unused; barbarians would turn their faces, and threats north of the desert would vanish like clouds.

sentences.zh: 安有周、秦、漢、魏優劣在其間哉。

translations.literal: How could there be Zhou, Qin, Han, and Wei with superiority and inferiority among them?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, Qin, Han, and Wei would not rank as better or worse.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.idiomatic: The full chapter is collated against the Zhonghua Shuju Book of Zhou, November 1971.
